title: Greg Pruitt's NFL Career: Five Pro Bowls and a Super Bowl Ring
question: What did Greg Pruitt do in the NFL after playing at Oklahoma?
answer: Greg Pruitt (OU 1970-72) was a 1973 second-round pick of the Cleveland Browns who made five Pro Bowls, four with Cleveland and one with the Raiders, and won Super Bowl XVIII with the Los Angeles Raiders.
summary: Former Sooner Greg Pruitt made five Pro Bowls with the Browns and Raiders and won Super Bowl XVIII. A look at the NFL career of OU's two-time All-American.
body: Before he ever wore a Browns helmet, Greg Pruitt (OU 1970-72) was a Houston kid who became one of the most electric runners in Sooner history. He was a two-time consensus All-American, finished third in the 1971 Heisman voting and second in 1972, and later entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1999.

Cleveland grabbed him in the second round of the 1973 draft, and he made the Pro Bowl as a rookie. He went again in 1974, 1976 and 1977, and starting in 1975 he ran off three straight 1,000-yard rushing seasons. A serious knee injury in 1979 changed his role, so he reinvented himself as a receiving back; his 65 catches in 1981 led every running back in the AFC. He left Cleveland with 5,496 rushing yards, the fourth-most by a running back in franchise history according to the Cleveland Sports Hall of Fame, which inducted him in 2003.

In 1982 the Browns traded him to the Raiders for an 11th-round pick, a deal that looks like a bargain in hindsight. From 1982 to 1984 Pruitt became a return specialist, piling up 138 punt returns for 1,348 yards and a touchdown. He earned a fifth Pro Bowl trip with the Raiders and was part of the team that won Super Bowl XVIII.

Here is a fun piece of Sooner trivia: that Super Bowl XVIII opponent, Washington, had another OU star on its roster in Joe Washington. Two former Sooner running backs ended up on opposite sidelines on the NFL's biggest stage, and it was Pruitt who went home with the ring.
